title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Section 2 of the notes ('Courbes relatives de type (0,4)'). The setting is a base S, implicitly over Z[1/2]. X is a P^1-bundle (a conic) over S, and (9) I ⊂ X is a relative effective divisor, finite étale of degree 4. In modern terms, X with I marked is a family of 4-pointed genus-0 curves whose points are unordered and only étale-locally distinguishable.

(10) G_I = Aut_S(I) is a finite étale group scheme that is étale-locally (S_4)_S. S_4 has a unique normal subgroup isomorphic to the Klein group, so G_I contains a unique normal subgroup V_I, locally isomorphic to (Z/2 x Z/2)_S. Since the Klein group acts simply transitively on 4 letters, I is a V_I-torsor.

Proposition. The action of V_I on I extends uniquely to an action of V_I on X. Classically: for 4 distinct points of P^1, each double transposition is induced by a unique element of PGL_2, because a Möbius map is determined by 3 points and cross-ratio invariance gives existence. For the points 0, ∞, 1, λ, the map z ↦ λ/z realises (0∞)(1λ). Uniqueness lets these local extensions descend.

NB. Since Aut((Z/2)^2) = GL_2(F_2) = S_3, a twisted form V of (Z/2)^2 is the same thing as the degree-3 étale cover V* = V minus its zero section, which Grothendieck also calls Σ_I. Geometrically this is the cubic resolvent: the three ways of splitting the 4 points into two pairs. Hence the datum of I (an S_4-form, with S_4 = V ⋊ S_3) is equivalent to two pieces of data:
- V, equivalently the degree-3 cover V*;
- a V-torsor I.

Embedding such a torsor I into a P^1-bundle X then amounts to two steps:
- first, making V act faithfully on X, which was classified in §1 through the 'octahedral structure' Δ = the 6 fixed points of the three involutions;
- second (continued on the next page), choosing a section of (X∖Δ)/V and taking I to be its inverse image.

The next page re-expresses everything as follows. Start from the degree-3 cover J ≅ V*, the conic Σ_J and its degree-3 divisor D_J. The data are then a V-torsor K together with the principal V-cover X* of Σ_J ∖ D_J obtained by twisting the canonical 2-abelian cover. This is a relative, twisted version of the Legendre λ-line covering of the cross-ratio/j picture.

The purpose is to build a modular description of elliptic curves in characteristic ≠ 2, through E → P^1 branched at 4 points with E[2] ≅ V_I.
errors: The line 'plus la donnée d'un torseur I sous V^*' must mean a torsor under V. V* is only a degree-3 étale cover, not a group scheme; this is a slip or ambiguous notation.

Implicitly 2 is assumed invertible (title of the cote). The Möbius extension of the Klein action actually works in all characteristics, but the octahedral picture with Δ of degree 6 étale needs char ≠ 2.
The machine transcription duplicates the line 'I dans un fibré en droites projectives X'.

ideas.what: S_4-form of 4 unordered étale points; canonical Klein subgroup V_I with I a V_I-torsor; cubic resolvent V* of degree 3
ideas.modern_name: S_4 = V_4 ⋊ S_3, cubic resolvent, twisted forms via nonabelian H^1

ideas.what: Unique extension of the Klein-group action on 4 points of P^1 to an action on the P^1-bundle
ideas.modern_name: Klein four-group of cross-ratio symmetries; level-2 structure / E[2] acting on the quotient line
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Klein); relative version standard in moduli theory

ideas.modern_name: stack M_{0,4}/S_4 related to the elliptic modular stack in char ≠ 2; Legendre family as twisted V-cover

missed.claim: A careful twisted-form (stack-theoretic, over an arbitrary base) dictionary between unordered 4-pointed conics, Klein-group actions on conics (octahedral structures), cubic resolvents and V-torsors, designed as a route to the moduli of elliptic curves away from 2. The individual facts are classical; the systematic relative presentation is an unpublished detail, but it does not appear to contain results unknown to specialists.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Of mainly historical interest. It shows Grothendieck around 1980–82 working concretely on the modular stack via the (0,4) ↔ elliptic link, contemporaneous with the Esquisse's focus on M_{0,4} and M_{1,1}.

deep.surprise_reason: Correct, careful but classical material: the Klein group in S_4, cross-ratio involutions and cubic resolvents, written in the relative/twisted language. It is interesting as context for the Esquisse's dessins and Teichmüller-tower interests, but contains nothing a specialist would find new.
